details.summary: This is a vibrant, appealing Mediterranean recipe that makes excellent use of quick-cooking halibut and whole-wheat couscous to deliver a well-balanced meal in under 30 minutes. A couple of minor adjustments—adding the missing salt and pepper to the ingredient list and slightly tweaking the couscous-to-spinach ratio to perfectly align with the fiber and carb targets—will make it an outstanding inclusion for the book.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is classically Mediterranean and beautifully balanced. The bright acidity of the lemon and tomatoes complements the umami from the olives and the garlic-oregano aromatic base, making perfect culinary sense with the mild halibut.

Step 2 mentions seasoning the halibut with 'black pepper, and a pinch of salt,' but neither salt nor black pepper is included in the ingredient list. Please add them to the ingredients to ensure strict consistency.

The instructions are excellent for a beginner cook. They include clear time ranges, prompt checks at the minimum times, and distinct visual doneness cues (golden, blister and burst, spinach wilts, completely opaque and flakes easily).

The recipe aligns perfectly with the stated Mediterranean cuisine style, relying on staple ingredients like extra-virgin olive oil, cherry tomatoes, garlic, oregano, olives, lemon, and whole-wheat couscous.
Searing the halibut on one side to develop flavor and then finishing it in a gentle simmer within the tomato pan sauce is an ideal technique to keep this lean fish moist and tender.

The computed macronutrients are completely consistent with the ingredient quantities. The protein aligns with 5 oz of halibut per serving, and the saturated fat reflects the use of a lean fish and extra-virgin olive oil.

The title faithfully reflects the dish, and the intro accurately highlights the main ingredients. The tone is warm and practical, successfully avoiding any banned health claims or 'diet food' language.
This is a highly appetizing, original, and well-thought-out weeknight meal. The vibrant blistered tomato sauce over fluffy couscous makes it visually appealing and deeply satisfying.

The recipe genuinely addresses both liver health and blood sugar management. It is strongly Mediterranean in character, leads with extra-virgin olive oil, features a lean protein, and relies on a clear, unrefined whole-grain carbohydrate.

There is zero added sugar in this recipe. Additionally, the inclusion of whole-wheat couscous ensures the dish provides a high-quality carbohydrate base, steering clear of any inappropriate 'keto' or extremely low-carb pitfalls.

The dish is mostly on-brief but slightly drifts past the tier's carbohydrate ceiling (57.5g vs 55g) and undershoots the fiber floor (6.2g vs 7g). Consider reducing the dry couscous to 1/2 cup (80g) and bumping the spinach up to 5 or 6 oz to land perfectly within the target window.
The recipe meets the 30-minute promise comfortably. Prep is minimal, active cooking time is around 14 minutes, there are no hidden waits, and all ingredients are everyday supermarket staples.
